content: In Ezekiel, what was the valley the Spirit set Ezekiel down in full of?
explanation: They were very dry. “and set me down in the middle of the valley, and it was full of bones.” (Ezekiel 37:1, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel's valley of dry bones, what did God ask him?
explanation: Ezekiel said only God knows. “Son of man, can these bones come to life?” (Ezekiel 37:3, BSB)

content: As Ezekiel prophesied to the dry bones, what did they do?
explanation: There was a rattling noise. “there was suddenly a noise, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.” (Ezekiel 37:7, BSB)

content: When breath entered the dry bones Ezekiel saw, what did they become?
explanation: They stood on their feet. “and they came to life and stood on their feet—a vast army.” (Ezekiel 37:10, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, God promises to replace a heart of stone with a heart of what?
explanation: He gives a new spirit. “I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.” (Ezekiel 36:26, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, how did the scroll God gave Ezekiel to eat taste?
explanation: God's word was sweet. “So I ate, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.” (Ezekiel 3:3, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, what does God say He Himself will search for?
explanation: Like a shepherd seeks sheep. “Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out.” (Ezekiel 34:11, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel's vision, which face did each living creature NOT have?
explanation: They also had an ox's face. “The form of their faces was that of a man, and each of the four had the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle.” (Ezekiel 1:10, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, what did God tell Ezekiel to eat before speaking to Israel?
explanation: God's words filled him. “Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.” (Ezekiel 3:1, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, what did God make Ezekiel for the house of Israel?
explanation: He warned them for God. “Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel.” (Ezekiel 3:17, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel's valley vision, from where was the breath to come?
explanation: So the slain might live. “Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live!” (Ezekiel 37:9, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, God takes no pleasure in anyone's death, so what does He urge?
explanation: God desires life. “So repent and live!” (Ezekiel 18:32, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel's vision, what happens wherever the river from the temple flows?
explanation: Even the waters become fresh. “so wherever the river flows, everything will flourish.” (Ezekiel 47:9, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, God searched for a man to stand where for the land?
explanation: But He found no one. “I searched for a man among them to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Me” (Ezekiel 22:30, BSB)
Ezekiel was a priest. “the word of the LORD came directly to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi” (Ezekiel 1:3, BSB)

content: By which river was Ezekiel among the exiles when he saw visions of God?
explanation: It was in the land of the Chaldeans. “while I was among the exiles by the River Kebar, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.” (Ezekiel 1:1, BSB)

content: At the end of Ezekiel, what will the city's new name be?
explanation: God dwells with His people. “and from that day on the name of the city will be: THE LORD IS THERE.” (Ezekiel 48:35, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, for how many days did Ezekiel lie on his left side for Israel?
explanation: A day for each year of iniquity. “For I have assigned to you 390 days, according to the number of years of their iniquity.” (Ezekiel 4:5, BSB)

content: In Ezekiel, what words were written on both sides of the scroll?
explanation: It was a hard message. “And written on the front and back of it were words of lamentation, mourning, and woe.” (Ezekiel 2:10, BSB)
